title: Welcome to my website!
text:

Welcome to my website!
Hello everyone!
My name is Aryan Pasricha, and I am originally from Toronto, Canada. I am currently a Research Coordinator at the Cleveland Clinic’s Heart, Vascular & Thoracic Institute (HVTI) and a part-time Master’s student in the Clinical Research Scholars Program (CRSP). My research focuses on aortic disease, particularly the perioperative care and outcomes of patients with aortic aneurysms and dissections.
I moved to Cleveland over a year ago and have really enjoyed exploring the city, especially its small local shops, bars, and coffee shops. I am also a music fanatic who loves playing the guitar and performing country music.
Outside of work and school, I have two older brothers who both live in New York City. One works as a journalist and broadcaster, while the other works in investment banking.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions or would like to discuss potential projects.

title: About Me
text:
I graduated from Wake Forest University with a Bachelor of Science, majoring in Health and Exercise Science and minoring in Chemistry and Entrepreneurship. Outside of the classroom, I was a member of both the Club Lacrosse and Basketball teams. I also served as President of an organization called Campus Kitchen, which focused on recovering and repurposing meals for individuals and families in the Winston-Salem community. Academically, I was involved in research examining treatment approaches for patients with hip osteopenia, specifically the effects of exercise interventions and pharmaceutical therapies. Some of my favorite experiences on campus were taking walks along the beautiful forest trails and attending sporting events.


Following my graduation in 2025, I began a gap year as a Research Assistant in the Roselli Lab at Cleveland Clinic, investigating aortic disease. I have since transitioned into a Research Coordinator role, taking on greater responsibilities in coordinating the lab’s research activities and overseeing multiple projects.
Our translational research combines biomechanical testing and bioengineering approaches to measure stress and strain in aortic tissue and correlate these findings with in vivo MRI measurements. The overarching goal is to improve the precision of surgical decision-making and timing by moving beyond aortic diameter as the sole determinant of surgical intervention.
In addition to this work, I am involved in several retrospective studies examining regional transfer times for patients with acute aortic dissection and the clinical implications of cerebral malperfusion following dissection.

title: NHL News
text:
As a Canadian and die-hard hockey fan, particularly of the Toronto Maple Leafs, I’ve always followed the NHL closely. The 2026–27 season has already been an eventful one, with several major trades, signings, and roster changes across the league. I wanted to highlight three moves that have particularly caught my attention, along with their potential impact on the teams involved and the broader NHL landscape.



Kirill Marchenko to the Toronto Maple Leafs: Toronto made a major statement by acquiring Kirill Marchenko from the Columbus Blue Jackets in a blockbuster deal that sent Matthew Knies the other way. Marchenko brings an exciting offensive presence to Toronto, but giving up a young power forward like Knies makes this a particularly fascinating gamble. As a Leafs fan, I’m interested to see whether this move can finally help push Toronto toward a deeper playoff run.
Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils: One of the biggest surprises of the season was Winnipeg trading superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey. A former Vezina Trophy winner, Hellebuyck gives the Devils an elite presence between the pipes and could be the missing piece for a team looking to establish itself as a legitimate Stanley Cup contender.
Brady Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers: Florida made a massive statement by acquiring Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk. Reuniting him with his brother Matthew creates an intimidating forward group and adds another layer of physicality and offensive firepower to an already competitive Panthers team. It will be interesting to see how this move impacts the balance of power in the Eastern Conference.
